events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your trip and you're getting a partial refund of $6.49. We looked at the GPS route and your chat messages. You agreed to one detour via a road you were asked about, and that part was fine. A second detour went a different way and wasn't covered by anything you agreed to, so you were charged for extra distance you shouldn't have paid for. The $6.49 goes back to the card or account you originally paid with. Only the extra distance is refunded; the time charge and platform fee stay as they are. No further action is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed this trip and found an issue with the route. One detour was covered by the rider's agreement, but a second detour took a different set of roads that wasn't covered. The roads on that stretch had no traffic hold-up, and no traffic reason was recorded, so you'll be sent a notification-duty reminder and this will be logged on your route compliance record, along with a violation for driving the segment without a traffic reason. As this is your first such incident, there's no formal warning and no account flag. $6.49 is being refunded to the rider's original payment method.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.49 to the rider's original payment method for the unconsented second off-route segment; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on the driver's route compliance record (first such incident: no formal warning); record a driver violation for the segment driven with no traffic reason under RD-2. Do not add an account flag (RD-6 threshold not met).
ruling.reasoning:
The record is complete and internal-consistent: two timestamped chat messages [F10], a full GPS track splitting the trip into two off-route segments [F3][F4], and a fare breakdown [F5][F7]. Deviation over 1 km is settled: +10.31 km, so RD-1's tolerance is passed [F1][RD-1]. The two segments total 10.44 km added (5.71 + 4.73) [F3][F4], and the trace's route-level deviation is 10.31 km [F1][F5]; I use the trace's 10.31 km in the RD-2 formula and assess each segment under RD-3 / RD-5.

F3 (22:54–23:03). The driver asked at 22:50 "can go via Upper Bukit Timah Road?" [F8] and the rider answered "ok" at 22:51 [F9] — before the segment began at 22:54, so the timing requirement of RD-5 is met, and a named road was agreed: UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD. Code checks the named road against the roads the segment drove (DAIRY FARM ROAD → UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD → JALAN ANAK BUKIT → DUNEARN ROAD → RIFLE RANGE ROAD) [F3]: the named road is among them, so the agreement covers the whole segment, including the roads before and after it that make up the way via X — ground named_road_tied, exempt. The driver's statement "She agreed to my route" [F11] is not relied on, and the rider's yes is not stretched to cover the later, differently-routed segment.

F4 (23:07–23:13). The only rider message is the 22:51 "ok" [F9], which agrees to a specific named road, UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD — not to whatever route was later taken. The roads this segment drove are ARCADIA ROAD → ADAM ROAD → LORNIE HIGHWAY → LORNIE ROAD → KHEAM HOCK ROAD → TREVOSE CRESCENT → MERRYN ROAD [F4]; the named road does not appear anywhere in them, so the agreement does not cover this segment — ground named_road_elsewhere, counts. RD-4 supports counting rather than excusing: the expressways were free-flowing at speed band 8 [F12][F13], no incident or congestion is recorded on the replaced stretch [F14], and the weather was fair [F15], so there is no traffic reason and RD-2 also requires a driver violation to be recorded.

Amount: (10.31 km deviation − 5.71 km exempt under RD-3/RD-5) × $1.4100/km = 4.60 km × $1.4100 = $6.486 → $6.49 [F1][F5][RD-2]. This is the trace's "F3 exempt, F4 counts" branch. Only excess distance fare is refunded; time fare and the platform fee are not [F7][RD-2]. Surge is nil, 1.0×, so no SURGE differential arises [F6].

No repeat-deviation flag: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so RD-6's condition is not met even though a violation is recorded for this trip. Under TH-1/TH-2 a route deviation under $10 is decided by the system, following DISP-001.

element_findings.reason: Not needed for the outcome: the scope of the 22:51 "ok" is read directly against the roads driven — tied for F3, elsewhere for F4 — so no segment is left undetermined.

I read every chat message, the driver's statement and the complaint: the driver's proposal and the rider's "ok" are an ordinary route exchange, the driver's statement is a factual claim about agreement, and the complaint is about the fare. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears [F8][F9][F11].

segment_findings.reason: The driver's 22:50 message proposed a specific road, Upper Bukit Timah Road, and the rider's 22:51 "ok" agrees to it — both before the segment began at 22:54, satisfying RD-5 timing [F8][F9][F10]. The named road is among the roads this segment drove (DAIRY FARM ROAD → UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD → JALAN ANAK BUKIT → DUNEARN ROAD → RIFLE RANGE ROAD), so the agreement covers the segment in full and it is not a deviation: exempt under RD-5 (RD-3 serves to exempt the agreed route).

The only prior rider agreement is the 22:51 "ok" to Upper Bukit Timah Road [F9]; that road is absent from the roads driven on this segment (ARCADIA ROAD → ADAM ROAD → LORNIE HIGHWAY → LORNIE ROAD → KHEAM HOCK ROAD → TREVOSE CRESCENT → MERRYN ROAD) [F4]. No rider message before 23:07 agrees to anything else, and the driver's post-trip statement [F11] is not consent. The segment is a refundable deviation under RD-2 / RD-5, with no traffic reason under RD-4 [F12][F13][F14].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's request for the whole extra distance fails for F3: the rider agreed before the segment to a route via Upper Bukit Timah Road [F9], which the segment drove, so its 5.71 km are exempt under RD-3/RD-5 [F3]. The refund is limited to the 4.60 km of the unagreed F4 segment [F4][RD-2].

The driver's claim, arising from his own statement "She agreed to my route" [F11], that the whole route was agreed fails: a post-trip statement is not prior consent [RD-5], and the rider's only agreement was to Upper Bukit Timah Road [F9], which is absent from the roads driven on F4 [F4].

Any claim that no traffic reason is needed to excuse the second detour fails: no incident or congestion is recorded on the replaced stretch [F14] and the expressways were free-flowing at speed band 8 [F12][F13], so RD-4 gives no exemption and RD-2 requires the excess distance fare to be refunded and a violation recorded.
